# PREFIX-783 — Private reflection defects are immaterial to pointwise two-sign persistence

Date: 2026-11-14. Scientific status: AUTHOR_PROVED / EXACT_RATIONAL_REGRESSION / UNREVIEWED / NOT_ADMITTED.
Prior frozen scientific input: `f42f2906d77f24085c123f3ccfe9667d41caa96d`.
Source lineage: PREFIX-782 (2026-11-14), `2026-11-14_r6_prefix782_shared_reflection_defect_pointwise_window.md`.
Source Researcher-ID: `EM-DIRECT-E77192`; historic activity `RA-66BBE259AEE1AD543D9454A3`. This is independent auxiliary-model work, not a native X6 CLAIM.

## 1. Setup and new question

Fix a real parameter \(q>0\). In the external 189-layer BRC–Gamma scalar auxiliary model, retain two adjacent diagonal \(1/768\) cells \(R_1=[38,39]^2/768\), \(R_2=[39,40]^2/768\) and their reflections under \(z\mapsto1-z\). The unperturbed normalized mixed differences of \(V_q=q^2\operatorname{Var}(Y)-q\mathbb E[Y]\) are \((x_1,x_2,-x_1,-x_2)\), with \(x_i=A_i-qB_i\), \(0<B_1<B_2\), as in PREFIX-782.

The two base cells share one corner; its normalized scalar errors are \(h\) and \(h'\) at the reflected pair. Assume \(|h|,|h'|\le c\), \(|h-h'|\le\delta\), with \(c,\delta\ge0\).

Each cell has three other, private corners. For each private corner \(j\) of cell \(i\), let \(\eta_{ij}\) and \(\eta'_{ij}\) be the base/reflected scalar errors, satisfying the *same* independent box bounds \(|\eta_{ij}|\le e_{ij}\) and \(|\eta'_{ij}|\le e_{ij}\). The two errors need not agree; any optional upper bounds on their difference may be imposed so long as equality is permitted. Let the corresponding signed corner sums be \(u_i=\sum_j\sigma_{ij}\eta_{ij}\) and \(u_i'=\sum_j\sigma_{ij}\eta_{ij}'\), where \(\sigma_{ij}\in\{-1,1\}\); put \(S_i=\sum_j e_{ij}\). The four observed mixed differences, divided by \(q\), are

\[
a_1=x_1+h+u_1,\quad a_2=x_2+h+u_2,\quad
a_3=-(x_1+h'+u_1'),\quad a_4=-(x_2+h'+u_2').
\]

The shared-corner signs and private-corner signs are inherited from the exact mixed-difference geometry. This is a scalar-corner perturbation class; there is no claimed native Cell/Link/Port observation map.

## 2. Symmetrization theorem (new)

**Theorem 783.1 (private-reflection saturation).** In the full independent private-corner box class above, a perturbation with four differences *not containing both a strictly positive and a strictly negative member* exists if and only if such a perturbation exists with **every private reflected error exactly equal to its base error** (\(\eta'_{ij}=\eta_{ij}\)). The theorem remains true after adding arbitrary nonnegative upper bounds \(|\eta_{ij}-\eta'_{ij}|\le d_{ij}\) to private pairs.

**Proof.** A finite real four-tuple fails to have both strict signs exactly when all four entries are nonnegative or all four are nonpositive.

Suppose first all \(a_k\ge0\). Since \(-S_i\le u_i,u_i'\le S_i\), the inequalities give
\(x_i+h\ge-S_i\) and \(x_i+h'\le S_i\).
Replace the shared values by \(H=\max(h,h')\), \(H'=\min(h,h')\). These values retain both box bounds and the same absolute shared difference, and satisfy \(H\ge H'\). The original inequalities imply
\(-x_i-H\le S_i\) and \(-x_i-H'\ge-S_i\).
Consequently the exact closed interval
\[
K_i=[-S_i,S_i]\cap[-x_i-H,-x_i-H']
\]
is nonempty. Pick any \(v_i\in K_i\). As \(|v_i|\le S_i=\sum_j e_{ij}\), allocate the signed sum \(v_i\) over the three private budgets (greedily in signed corner coordinates, or by interval Minkowski addition). Use the *same* allocated errors on each reflected private partner, so that \(u_i=u_i'=v_i\). The resulting tuple has
\(x_i+H+v_i\ge0\) and \(-(x_i+H'+v_i)\ge0\) for both \(i\); hence it is all-nonnegative and satisfies even zero private reflection defects.

For an all-nonpositive tuple, put \(H=\min(h,h')\) and \(H'=\max(h,h')\). Then the original inequalities yield \(x_i+H\le S_i\), \(x_i+H'\ge-S_i\), and
\[
K_i=[-S_i,S_i]\cap[-x_i-H',-x_i-H]\ne\varnothing.
\]
Choosing and duplicating \(v_i\in K_i\) gives \(x_i+H+v_i\le0\) and \(-(x_i+H'+v_i)\le0\). The converse holds by inclusion of the equal-private class in the unrestricted class. The optional private difference bounds also hold after symmetrization because their left sides vanish. QED.

**Corollary 783.2 (exact maximal private-defect robustness).** For every fixed real \(q>0\), even with *unrestricted* reflected private-corner differences, the existence of a sign-loss observer is characterized by the same three inequalities as PREFIX-782:
\[
\boxed{\ |x_1|\le S_1+c,\qquad
|x_2|\le S_2+c,\qquad
|x_1-x_2|\le S_1+S_2+\min(\delta,2c)\ }.
\]
If any one inequality fails, every observer with these symmetric per-corner budgets has a strictly positive and a strictly negative mixed difference.

For completeness, the equal-private proof is an exact interval reduction. Write \(r=H-H'\in[0,\min(\delta,2c)]\), \(s=(H+H')/2\). Sign loss with all nonnegative entries is possible precisely when the three intervals
\[
[-c+r/2,c-r/2],\
[-x_1-S_1-r/2,-x_1+S_1+r/2],\
[-x_2-S_2-r/2,-x_2+S_2+r/2]
\]
have a common point. Pairwise intersection of real intervals is equivalent to the three boxed conditions with \(r\) replacing \(\min(\delta,2c)\) in the last one. Thus choose \(r=\max(0,|x_1-x_2|-S_1-S_2)\); when the boxed conditions hold, \(r\) lies in the admissible range and any common \(s\) gives a constructive observer. The all-nonpositive case is symmetric.

**Corollary 783.3 (positive-\(q\) window).** For \(x_i(q)=A_i-qB_i\), \(0<B_1<B_2\), set \(T_i=S_i+c\) and \(U=S_1+S_2+\min(\delta,2c)\). The exact positive-parameter sign-loss set for the unrestricted private class is
\[
(0,\infty)\cap
[(A_1-T_1)/B_1,(A_1+T_1)/B_1]\cap
[(A_2-T_2)/B_2,(A_2+T_2)/B_2]\cap
[(A_2-A_1-U)/(B_2-B_1),(A_2-A_1+U)/(B_2-B_1)].
\]
This is a pointwise existential classification: the observer may depend on \(q\). Equality cases belong to the sign-loss set.

## 3. Exact worked example and strength

Reuse PREFIX-782's independent rational instance \(A_1=1,A_2=2,B_1=2,B_2=3,S_1=1/5,S_2=3/20,c=1/10\). At \(q=3/5\), \(x_1=-1/5,x_2=1/5\). When \(\delta=0\), \(|x_1-x_2|=2/5>7/20=S_1+S_2\); therefore **all** permitted private-reflection errors retain both strict signs, even if the two sides are chosen completely independently. For example, \(h=h'=0\), \((u_1,u'_1)=(1/5,-1/5)\) and \((u_2,u'_2)=(-3/20,3/20)\) yield \((a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)=(0,1/20,2/5,-7/20)\). The private defects can change magnitudes but not the existential two-sign threshold.

When \(\delta=1/10\), the same \(q=3/5\) is in the sign-loss interval, and PREFIX-782's equal-private construction realizes \((0,1/20,1/20,0)\). In particular, measuring all six private reflection defects is **unnecessary for the binary sign-persistence decision** under the symmetric, independently selectable scalar corner budgets. These defects can matter for quantitative margin, correlated/one-sided measurement restrictions and native observer fidelity; none of those stronger quantities is identified with the binary theorem.

## 4. Verification, provenance and next scientific question

Companion program `PREFIX783_R6_UNRESTRICTED_PRIVATE_REFLECTION_CHECK.py` uses exact Python `fractions.Fraction` to test 4,096 seeded rational coefficient/budget/parameter cases. It compares the three-inequality test with a separately coded exact three-interval feasibility oracle, constructs real corner assignments for every feasible case, checks all mixed signs, and includes equality and the worked example. Machine result: `ALL_CHECKS_PASS PREFIX783 PRIVATE_REFLECTION_SYMMETRIZATION`. This finite regression is a check of the implementation and examples; Theorem 783.1 is proved for arbitrary real parameters by the order-preserving symmetrization argument.

Scientific references: PREFIX-782 at `enterprise-math` main (original paper blob `37ec3608c4bc109cdd5821bf3a55ef42846878d8`), PREFIX-781 at immutable commit `7d70facce45b39ab1ee764ec6ff2ca118f4ef379`; frozen input pin maintained. No new native BRC arithmetic, Gamma recurrence or source coefficients were computed, and no native comparator grid exclusion is added.

Next: identify whether a native BRC/X6 scalar observation offers *independently selectable, reflection-symmetric corner error boxes*; if it produces correlated, signed-source, non-box, or non-symmetric restrictions, derive a native-faithful sign-loss polytope instead of applying the present saturation theorem. Retain Cell, Link, Port, branch, provenance and event time for that comparison.
